hook: Minimising your tax now can cost you a house later.
so_what: Self-employed and buying within two years? Ask your accountant how your next return will read to a bank.

myth: Building a few townhouses means you need a private lender.
reality: A first small project usually fits a normal construction loan.
because: Two or three dwellings on reasonably priced land can often go mainstream. Same result, without a couple of percent extra in private rates and fees.

text:
Different banks win at different things.

The lender with the sharpest rate for your refinance often isn’t the one that will lend you the most for your next purchase.

So we might refinance you with one bank and fund the next purchase with another.

One bank for everything is tidy. Matching each loan to the bank that’s best at that job usually serves you better.

label: investing
hook: If you can afford it, buy the house.
sub: And why cheap isn’t the same as good value.

label: investing
title: Houses usually grow faster
body: If the budget stretches, a house beats a unit as an investment almost every time. In many family-oriented regional markets, renters want houses too.

label: investing
title: When a unit makes sense
body: When borrowing capacity forces it, or it’s a genuinely exceptional deal. Otherwise, ask what a house in a proven area costs before you settle.

label: investing
title: Cheap towns carry risk
body: A small town that just looks cheap may not grow at all. Thin markets have little data behind the price. The same budget often buys better somewhere proven.

label: investing
headline: House or unit? Proven or cheap?
body: A 15-minute chat is enough to know where you stand.
